answer: Each epoch auctions just 100 new identity slots. An applicant locks a copper bond as its bid; the top 100 bids win, the rest refunded. A walnut-shell identity is free to mint, so the auction is the defence: one fake pays the 100th bid, ten fakes must outbid each other and push the clearing price up, so cost per fake rises with each fake bought. Like a glacier the queue moves slowly: winners wait a full epoch before earning, and duplicates lose bond and slot.
